summary.headline: Eternal's Q2FY27 call was Q&A-only: management kept FY29 $1B Adjusted EBITDA guidance and flagged food margins flat for 1-2 years while reinvesting in growth.
summary.overview: The call covered only the Q&A session, with no prepared remarks or reported financial figures in the transcript. Management said competitive intensity in food delivery rose in Q2 and that Eternal is investing more in customer acquisition and frequency, with margins expected to stay broadly flat over the next 1-2 years. In quick commerce, management said the 12-month competitive spike is over, which gives it confidence to re-accelerate store expansion, mainly in smaller cities, starting October-December quarter. Management also discussed dark.ai, a privacy-focused AI application for power users, which is unmonetised and carried in the Others segment.

segments.name: Food delivery
segments.commentary: Competitive intensity was higher in Q2 than in prior quarters, partly driven by Zomato's own investments. Management expects margins to stay broadly flat over the next 1-2 years and will reinvest surplus into growth. Management declined to comment on whether 22-23% YoY growth is a fair assumption for 2H.

segments.name: Quick commerce (Blinkit)
segments.commentary: Management plans to accelerate store additions from the October-December quarter, mostly in smaller cities, and expects no short-term margin hit. NOV per store per day is about INR 9 lakh versus a steady-state target of about INR 11 lakh. Blinkit's 1P share is at a steady state of about 90-95% of SKUs. Store capex guidance of INR 2.5 crore is a blended figure.

segments.name: Others (dark.ai and enterprise AI)
segments.commentary: dark.ai has been in development for about a year, is unmonetised and is carried in Others, with costs described as not yet meaningful. Management said the base case is a high gross margin business, but hardware and compute may be needed if demand is strong. Launch is a few months away.

guidance_outlook: Management maintains the FY29 $1 billion Adjusted EBITDA guidance, but said it is too early to comment on it further.
Food delivery margins are expected to remain broadly flattish over the next 1-2 years, with investment in growth prioritised over margin optimisation.
Quick commerce store additions are to accelerate from the October-December quarter, with NOV growth expected to pick up on a YoY basis in that quarter.
Management expects the bulk of new quick commerce stores to be in smaller cities, and expects Blinkit's NOV per store per day to rise over time, though not linearly.
dark.ai launch is a few months away; monetisation and capex decisions will be taken closer to launch.
capex_capacity: Blinkit blended capex per new store is about INR 2.5 crore, and tier 2 and tier 3 stores are expected to cost less, but management did not confirm a separate figure.
Store additions are set to nearly double over the next 6-7 quarters, with the bulk in smaller cities.
NOV per store per day is about INR 9 lakh today versus a steady-state target of about INR 11 lakh; management said growth in store numbers may be lumpy.
dark.ai capex is not expected to be meaningful unless the product gets a very strong response, in which case GPUs and infrastructure may be needed.
Quick commerce SKU mix is at a steady state of 90-95% 1P, so no further incremental working capital build is expected from that.
demand_pricing: Food delivery competitive intensity was higher in Q2, and Eternal is raising investment in new customer acquisition and frequency.
Quick commerce competition rose over the past 12 months with 5-7 players; management says it now has better visibility on competitor strategies.
Blinkit NOV growth is expected to pick up YoY from the October-December quarter. Blinkit's MTU in mature cities is multiple times Zomato's MTU, with no plateau seen yet.

Mature cities (operating more than 2-3 years) account for over 70% of NOV that is EBITDA positive; the share of NOV from top 8 cities is declining directionally, and management did not disclose the figure.
New cities have NAOV about 10-15% lower; assortment expansion in tier 1 cities offsets this. Gourmet stores have expanded to Bengaluru and Mumbai but are not a material share of orders.

qa_highlights.question: Has food delivery discounting intensified in Q2, and have margins peaked?
qa_highlights.answer: Competitive intensity was higher than in prior quarters, partly driven by Zomato. Management expects margins to stay broadly flattish over 1-2 years and to reinvest surplus in growth.

qa_highlights.question: Why accelerate quick commerce store additions in FY28, and where?
qa_highlights.answer: Competition is now more predictable after the 12-month spike. Most new stores will be in smaller cities, where payback is described as strong.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Blinkit contribution margin trend despite NOV per store rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed flat contribution to investment in new stores. NOV per store does not translate linearly into contribution because store size and gross profit mix also vary.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FY29 $1B Adjusted EBITDA guidance more comfortable given better competition visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to comment beyond maintaining the guidance, noting that only two quarters of the three-year plan have passed.

qa_highlights.question: What is dark.ai, what is its capex and monetisation, and is it within Eternal?
qa_highlights.answer: dark.ai is inside Eternal and unmonetised, with costs carried in Others. It is an application layer on open-source models, with the base case being a high gross margin, self-funding business. Hosting may need GPUs if demand is strong.

qa_highlights.question: Will tier 2 and tier 3 store capex be below INR 2.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: The INR 2.5 crore figure is blended across tiers, set with the expectation that most expansion would be in tier 2 cities.

risks_watch: Food delivery competition could keep discounting elevated, which would pressure margins despite the flat-margin stance.
Blinkit store expansion could weigh on contribution margins in the short term and on NOV per store if new-store ramp is slower.
Blinkit's 79% growth reference point and the October-December NOV pickup need to be checked in the next quarterly update.
dark.ai launch timing, monetisation model and possible GPU capex are undefined; commitment to return on capital will be tested.
Share of NOV from top 8 cities is declining; management did not disclose the figure, so the mix shift is hard to track.
Exchange-rate exposure on dollar-priced tech server costs below contribution could raise indirect costs as the business scales.
summary.management_tone: Confident on quick commerce expansion and the competitive backdrop, but guarded on margins, the FY29 guidance and dark.ai monetisation. Management frequently declined to share specific figures, such as the top-8 city NOV share and the 2H food delivery growth assumption.
key_quotes: Directionally, we want to maintain margins broadly and reinvest in growth as much as it makes sense to continue to drive the growth upwards.
Doing this last year would have been fraught with risk because we didn't know how some of these things would have panned out, and payback on investments are very important for us.
If it works, it will become really big; it's more like a zero-to-one bet at this point.

adds.what: Blinkit dark store additions, nearly doubling over next 6-7 quarters, mostly smaller cities

growth.why: FY29 $1B Adjusted EBITDA guidance held and Blinkit store additions set to nearly double over 6-7 quarters from October-December, with NOV growth expected to pick up YoY; backing is partly specific (store count doubling, 2.5 crore blended capex per store) but there are no reported revenue figures and food margins are guided flat.
